lines.1: 「But... you went so far as to lay your past bare for me.」
lines.2: 「I think that was your kindness as a teacher, trying to persuade me not to get attached to someone like you.」
lines.3: 「That was part of it. But I also find excessive interference rather annoying.」
lines.9: 「It's about as full as it could possibly be.」
lines.10: 「I like moonlit nights like this... They make my heart dance, somehow.」
lines.14: 「The other boys got in our way at the sports festival, but nobody's here now.」
lines.17: 「We were supposed to dance at the sports festival.」
lines.18: 「True... But can you dance without any music, Tsushima?」
lines.21: 「Then I shall somehow be your partner.」
lines.24: 「There. Do not step on my feet.」
lines.25: 「Wait, Ms. Inori, you're unexpectedly good at this...」
lines.26: 「It is one of a lady's accomplishments.」
lines.28: 「...That face you make while stretching to keep up with an adult is rather sweet.」
lines.33: 「Someone who thinks, 'You are my everything,' would be too intense for me to date.」
lines.34: 「If someone leaned on me for comfort, I would fall over.」
lines.35: 「But neither would I lean on someone else and entrust myself to them.」
lines.36: 「I am difficult... Neither a pessimist nor an optimist.」
lines.37: 「You are still a hot-blooded student. Could someone like me truly satisfy you?」
lines.38: 「It's not a question of being satisfied...」
lines.39: 「You live by the mature style I wanted but could never achieve. I think that's wonderful.」
lines.40: 「I suspect it is something other than maturity...」
lines.41: 「Can I ask you one more thing?」
lines.42: 「About being from Mount Senjo in Oeyama...」
lines.43: 「Oh, that was a joke because the place happened to share my surname.」
lines.44: 「I am actually from the city, near Kyoto Station.」
lines.46: 「How are you so good at fortune-telling?」
lines.47: 「I have practiced since I was very young... It is no different from knowing a great deal about penny candy.」
lines.48: 「Honestly, where did you get that monstrous bird?」
lines.50: 「I was wandering through the night stalls in search of penny candy when I felt a damp, indecent gaze...」
lines.51: 「Its source was a bird sitting in a cage.」
lines.52: 「Little bird, little bird, why are you looking at me?」
lines.53: 「That way of thinking isn't cool... You're the one looking at me.」
lines.55: 「Hey, miss. What do you think? That parrot's awfully smart.」
lines.56: 「But as a display bird, his face is a fatal flaw... He's the only one I haven't sold.」
lines.57: 「And you're a beauty. I'll give you a good price.」
lines.59: 「Wait! I was interested in your breasts--ahem, no, your heart. That is why I was looking.」
lines.61: 「Indeed. I look like I know my language arts, do I not? I can tell what you're thinking. I can share your troubles.」
lines.62: 「I see it clearly: every night you soak your pillow with tears over romantic troubles.」
lines.64: 「Wait, please wait! I'll give you my food! Just hear me out!」
lines.66: 「Then I shall buy that parrot for 105 yen.」
lines.67: 「105 yen? That's cheaper than a candy apple!」
lines.71: 「Do you not find it presumptuous to haggle down the price of a life?」
lines.73: 「I cost the same as a piece of bubble gum?!」
lines.76: 「However romantic or mysterious something may seem, once you learn the trick, it amounts to no more than this. Are you disappointed?」
lines.77: 「No. I'm glad you feel more approachable now.」
lines.79: 「...This doesn't count as our date, does it?」
lines.81: 「Very well. School is about to enter recess... Fortune has favored the timing.」
lines.82: Ms. Inori gives a quiet chuckle.
lines.83: I feel myself drawn toward that smile.
